findings.title: Switch/binary_sensor/button module docstrings undercount their own entity rosters by 7
findings.claim: The module docstrings of switch.py, binary_sensor.py and button.py describe 1, 3 and 2 entities respectively, but each module's async_setup_entry registers 4, 5 and 4 -- seven entities the docstring prose does not mention.
findings.mechanism: The platform docstrings were written when each platform published fewer entities and were not revised when entities were added: switch.py says 'Provides an on/off switch' (OptimizerEnableSwitch) but also adds AwaySwitch, BoostDhwSwitch, BoostSpaceSwitch; binary_sensor.py enumerates exactly three bullet states but also adds VentilationBinarySensor and WoodCheaperBinarySensor; button.py names 'forcing an optimization run and starting a system-identification experiment' (two) but also adds DiagnoseIntervalButton and ResetComfortWeightButton. A reader who trusts the module docstring gets a wrong roster; docs/architecture.md and README list the correct 4/5/4, so the docstrings contradict the docs.

evidence.contention_note: 13 concurrent audit sessions on the box at take time (load1 ~34); the metric is an integer count of objects passed to async_add_entities, immune to contention

perturbation.change: append one extra entity to the list each async_setup_entry publishes (the harness applies it in memory with a sentinel, since the tree is read-only)
perturbation.observed_value: registered rises by exactly 1 per platform (switch 4->5, binary_sensor 5->6, button 4->5) and docstring_entity_gap by exactly 1

findings.metric_definition: per platform module: the count of entity objects the executed async_setup_entry hands to async_add_entities, minus the count the module's own docstring prose declares

null_control.note: the unperturbed async_setup_entry is run twice per module; the delta between the two runs is 0 for all three platforms

findings.proposed_fix_scope: docstring prose only in the three platform modules (no code change): state the real roster or drop the enumerations

findings.title: __init__.py lazy-import note understates the graph: says 40 modules, reaches 45
findings.claim: The lazy-import note in __init__.py says importing 'coordinator' and 'services' reaches 40 of the integration's modules, but doing so reaches 45 of the 62 sibling modules at runtime and 45 in the static import closure; the same stale 40 appears twice in the file.
findings.mechanism: The count in the anti-import-closure comment was accurate when written and was not updated as modules were added under coordinator.py; the comment's load-bearing point (importing the package must not execute that graph) still holds, but the number a reader would use to reason about the closure is now wrong by at least 3 and by 5 under the comment's own transitive reading.

evidence.contention_note: 13 concurrent audit sessions at take time (load1 ~21-34); an integer sys.modules count, immune to contention

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.coordinator (module import) and heatpump_optimizer.services (module import); the note sits at custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/__init__.py:54 and :63

perturbation.change: add one module-level relative import of a currently-unreached sibling to coordinator.py (e.g. 'from . import binary_sensor')
perturbation.observed_value: in-memory arm imported an unreached sibling and reachable rose 45->46; likewise the count falls by one if a sibling import is removed

findings.metric_definition: sibling .py modules of heatpump_optimizer (excluding __init__) present in sys.modules after a fresh process imports .coordinator then .services; plus the same over the static relative-import closure

null_control.note: the harness asserts the package is unimported before measuring and that importing an already-reached sibling adds nothing; the reachable set is a set, so a repeat import is a no-op (delta 0)

reproduction_steps: read reachable_sibling_modules=45 and static_closure_sibling_modules=45 against cited_in_init_comment=40
findings.proposed_fix_scope: comment text only, at __init__.py:54 and :63 (replace '40' with the measured number, or drop the figure)

findings.title: Two hand-maintained 'How the pieces fit' diagrams, already diverged
findings.claim: README.md and docs/architecture.md each carry a separate hand-maintained mermaid diagram under the heading 'How the pieces fit'; they share only 14 of 43 and 41 non-trivial lines and have already drifted in node set and edge sense, so the same heading shows two different graphs.
findings.mechanism: The diagram exists twice, once as the README overview and once as the architecture document's figure, with no include mechanism. Measured drift: README has a distinct 'weather' input node folded into 'ha' in architecture.md; README draws the Open-Meteo edge dotted ('irradiance override', optional) where architecture.md draws it solid; the safety-layer node's contents differ ('peak guard, fuse, manual-plan pins' vs 'power_guard, manual_plan, away, external_heat'). A reader comparing the two canonical docs is shown two different pictures of one system.

evidence.contention_note: 13 concurrent audit sessions at take time (load1 ~39); a set-intersection count over two files, immune to contention

findings.instrumented_symbol: n/a (text instrument): README.md mermaid block under 'How the pieces fit' vs the same block in docs/architecture.md; no production symbol is hooked

perturbation.change: re-word one shared node label in either diagram (verified on a transient copy of README.md, not in the export)

findings.metric_definition: identical non-trivial lines (whitespace-stripped, blank/fence/opener lines dropped) shared by the two mermaid blocks under the heading 'How the pieces fit'

null_control.note: deterministic text read; two runs give 14 both times. Caveat: the two-block design may be intentional (README summary vs architecture detail), in which case the defect is the drift, not the duplication.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: docs prose: keep one canonical diagram and link to it, or reconcile the two so they show the same graph
